draft.title: Collision theory
card: For a reaction to happen, reactant particles must collide. Most collisions do not lead to a reaction.
the colliding particles must have at least the activation energy, the minimum energy needed to break bonds and start the reaction.
the particles must hit each other at the right angle, so the atoms that must bond or break are brought together.
A collision with enough energy and the right orientation is a successful collision. Only successful collisions form products.
draft.remember: A reaction needs a collision that has both enough energy and the right orientation.

a.q: Two gas molecules collide with more than the activation energy, but with the wrong orientation. What happens?
opts: The collision is unsuccessful and no products form
The collision is successful and products form
The molecules react after they bounce apart
The molecules react because the energy is high enough
a.why: A successful collision needs both enough energy and the right orientation. Here the orientation is wrong, so no products form, even though the energy is enough.
a.clue: A successful collision needs two things at once.

b.q: In a flask, hydrogen and iodine gases collide very often, yet only a small fraction of collisions form hydrogen iodide. Which reason fits the collision theory?
opts: Most collisions lack enough energy or the right orientation
Most collisions happen between particles that do not touch
Most collisions use up the activation energy of the flask
Most collisions make products that at once change back
b.why: Only collisions with at least the activation energy and the right orientation are successful. Many collisions fail one of these tests, so only a small fraction form products. Collisions happening often does not make them successful.
b.clue: Think about what a collision must have to be successful.

a.best: The collision is unsuccessful and no products form

b.best: Most collisions lack enough energy or the right orientation
